# Group-aware policy

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:identity-policy` · **Epic:** [#59](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/59) · **Tickets:** 5 (1S 4M)

Allow rules, MCP tool allow conditions and per-tool constraints can be limited to IdP groups or specific users with `groups: [...]` / `users: [...]`. Rules without these fields behave exactly as today. A group-scoped rule never matches a request without a verified identity, so default-deny is preserved. Policy replay in `internal/policyeval` understands the new matchers.

## How we build it

- Schema: `AllowlistEntry.Groups []string` and `AllowlistEntry.Users []string` (sub or email), in yaml and json with omitempty. `MCPToolCondition` gains `Groups` and `Users` next to `AgentID`/`TimeWindow`. The denylist stays global in P1.
- Evaluator: add `policy.Subject{Sub, Email, Groups}` and `Evaluator.EvaluateFor(domain, port, scheme, *Subject)`. `Evaluate` becomes `EvaluateFor(..., nil)`. An entry with groups/users matches only if the subject is non-nil and shares a group or lists the user. Rate-limit keys stay per entry (per-user limits come in Phase 3).
- Request-time evaluation: when the CONNECT has no identity (X-Warden-Identity comes later), entries scoped to groups count as `Conditional`. With TLS termination the CONNECT proceeds and `identityStage` re-evaluates with the subject, and the request is denied if nothing matches. Without a CA, Conditional is a deny.
- MCP: the gateway `OnRequest` receives the subject through a new field on the proxy->gateway call (MCPGateway seam). `compileConditions` adds group/user sets, and the tool is denied with reason `mcp_tool_denied` when the condition fails.
- `policyeval.Evaluate` builds a Subject from `Event.UserSub/UserEmail/UserGroups` when replaying and reports regressions per user. The dashboard policy editor shows and edits groups/users chips.

## Done when

A rule `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}` allows a member of eng and denies a non-member and an anonymous request, both at CONNECT and via X-Warden-Identity, and `warden eval` replay shows which users a candidate change affects.

### 1/5 · W-P1-GPOL-01

**Add groups/users to allow entries and MCP conditions schema**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#60](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/60)

Add `Groups`/`Users` to `config.AllowlistEntry` and `config.MCPToolCondition` plus their raw YAML structs. Validate non-empty, trimmed values, deduplicate them, and lowercase emails in Users. Update `configs/config.example.yaml` with a commented example. Workers that predate this field would ignore it and over-allow, so the CP refuses to serve group-scoped entries to workers whose heartbeat reports a version without the `groupPolicy` capability. Add a `capabilities` field to the heartbeat body for this.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] YAML and JSON round-trip tests cover the new fields
- [ ] The CP logs and marks a worker `incompatible` in the fleet view when it lacks the capability and policy contains group-scoped entries

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-GPOL-02`](identity-policy.md#25--w-p1-gpol-02) Make the policy evaluator subject-aware with EvaluateFor

### 2/5 · W-P1-GPOL-02

**Make the policy evaluator subject-aware with EvaluateFor**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#61](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/61)

In `internal/policy/policy.go`, add `Subject`, `EvaluateFor` and a `Conditional` Decision that is returned only when a group-scoped entry would match the destination but the subject is nil. Keep `Evaluate` semantics identical for policies without scoped entries. Precompile the group/user sets in `load()`. Table tests cover member, non-member, nil subject and mixed scoped/unscoped entries.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The existing policy tests pass unchanged
- [ ] A nil subject against a scoped-only match returns Conditional, never Allow
- [ ] A benchmark shows no regression over 5% for unscoped policies

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-01`](identity-policy.md#15--w-p1-gpol-01) Add groups/users to allow entries and MCP conditions schema

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-GPOL-03`](identity-policy.md#35--w-p1-gpol-03) Apply group-aware allow decisions at CONNECT and request time; [`W-P1-GPOL-04`](identity-policy.md#45--w-p1-gpol-04) Support groups/users in MCP tool conditions and constraints

### 3/5 · W-P1-GPOL-03

**Apply group-aware allow decisions at CONNECT and request time**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#62](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/62)

In `handleConn`, call `EvaluateFor` with the CONNECT subject. Treat `Conditional` like NoMatch when TLS termination is available (proceed to TLS) and as deny otherwise. In `identityStage`, re-evaluate with the request subject when the CONNECT decision was Conditional. Deny with 403, Reason `group_not_allowed`, and the user fields when nothing matches. The judge is not consulted for Conditional-then-denied requests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An eng member is allowed and a non-member is denied, over both Proxy-Authorization and X-Warden-Identity
- [ ] Without a CA, a Conditional CONNECT is denied with 403
- [ ] An anonymous request to a group-only destination is denied in attribute mode

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-02`](identity-policy.md#25--w-p1-gpol-02) Make the policy evaluator subject-aware with EvaluateFor; [`W-P1-VRFY-02`](identity-verification.md#25--w-p1-vrfy-02) Extract, verify and strip identity on CONNECT and requests

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-GPOL-05`](identity-policy.md#55--w-p1-gpol-05) Teach policyeval replay and the dashboard editor about groups

### 4/5 · W-P1-GPOL-04

**Support groups/users in MCP tool conditions and constraints**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#63](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/63)

Extend the proxy->gateway seam so `Gateway.OnRequest` receives the request subject. Extend `compiledCondition` with group and user sets in `compileConditions`, so `AllowWhen{groups:[...]}` gates a tool per user, and scope constraints keyed to such tools are applied the same way. A failing condition denies the tool with `mcp_tool_denied` in enforce mode and is recorded in monitor mode.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A `tools/call` for a tool gated to group finance is denied for eng and allowed for finance in enforce mode
- [ ] The existing gateway and scopes tests pass, and a nil subject never satisfies a group condition

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-02`](identity-policy.md#25--w-p1-gpol-02) Make the policy evaluator subject-aware with EvaluateFor; [`W-P1-VRFY-03`](identity-verification.md#35--w-p1-vrfy-03) Record user fields on events, receipts, logs and fleet ingest

### 5/5 · W-P1-GPOL-05

**Teach policyeval replay and the dashboard editor about groups**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#64](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/64)

In `internal/policyeval/eval.go`, build a `policy.Subject` from each event's user fields and evaluate with `EvaluateFor`. Add `AffectedUsers` (distinct sub/email) to each regression entry in `EvalResult`, and print it in `warden eval` output. In the dashboard policy editor, add groups/users chip inputs per allow entry and show a 'scoped' badge in the policy view.

**Acceptance criteria**
